coder_notes: Strong hygiene on everything around the split except the split mechanism itself: near-duplicates were screened with 64-bit pHash (Hamming distance <= 4) and removed BEFORE partitioning, the hard-positive subset is drawn only from the test set and explicitly excluded from training/validation/selection, and all comparison models share the same split and protocol. A genuine cross-dataset test is reported (train on UFFS, evaluate on Wildfire Smoke V1 with no fine-tuning) but the resulting numbers are not in the excerpt, so cross_dataset_delta is not_reported. The paper is unusually candid that its 87 FPS came from an RTX 3090 Ti desktop and is not evidence of onboard UAV performance. coder_notes: The only stated partitioning mechanism is cross-validation whose folds were 'stratified by ignition date and case number'. I coded k_fold_random because stratification balances cases ACROSS folds rather than holding whole cases out; the paper never states that a wildfire case sits in only one fold, so group_disjoint is not established. That same ambiguity is why leakage_risk is medium and not high: read as stratification, pixels from each of the 62 wildfire cases appear on both sides of every fold, which would be the 'same event both sides' case; read as grouping, it would be low. One mitigation the paper does report: a 15x15 window centred on each KFS fire location was omitted when extracting nonfire samples. comparison_is_like_for_like = no because the cross-validated LGBM (trained on folds of the very cases it is scored on) is tabulated against the operational GK-2A FF product, which never trained on them. Clouds are handled by exclusion, not tested: only 'noncloud-contaminated' wildfires were analysed and cloud-covered pixels are dropped from the model output, hence adverse_weather_tested = no. A transferability test in southwestern China is reported, but its numbers are not in the excerpt, so cross_dataset_delta stays not_reported.
